high.title: Why Loan Interest Rates Haven't Fallen? The Answer Lies in the Selic
high.summary: The Central Bank's analysis reveals why credit remains expensive in Brazil despite monetary policy easing, pointing to structurally high Selic rates as the primary culprit rather than fiscal imbalances alone. The BCB's Credit Cost Indicator (ICC) shows the effective average cost of the entire National Financial System's credit stock, reflecting banks' average margins over funding costs across all outstanding contracts, not just new loans. This comprehensive metric demonstrates how elevated Selic levels create economic distortions that prevent credit cost reductions from reaching consumers and businesses. For BRL traders, this analysis is crucial as it suggests monetary policy transmission mechanisms remain impaired, potentially limiting the effectiveness of rate cuts in stimulating economic activity. Bond investors should note that persistent high credit spreads may signal continued monetary policy challenges, while the structural nature of these issues could keep the BCB more hawkish for longer than markets expect.

high.title: Economists Adjust 2026 Inflation Projection; See Monday's Focus (27th)
high.summary: The Central Bank's Focus survey shows economists raising 2026 IPCA inflation forecasts from 4.80% to 4.86%, now above the BCB's tolerance range, signaling persistent inflationary pressures. Selic rate expectations remain unchanged at 13% for 2026 and 11% for 2027, while USD/BRL forecasts improved slightly to R$5.25 by year-end from previous projections. The upward inflation revision beyond the target ceiling suggests markets expect the BCB to maintain a restrictive monetary stance longer, supporting BRL bonds but potentially limiting equity upside. FX traders should note the modest dollar forecast improvement despite inflation concerns, indicating expectations that monetary tightness will eventually contain price pressures while supporting the Real.

medium.title: Ibovespa Rally Doesn't Eliminate 'Invisible Risk': Meet Empiricus' New Global Allocation Portfolio to 'Shield' Your Portfolio
medium.summary: The Ibovespa has surged 20% year-to-date, reaching new highs near 198,000 points, driven by R$50 billion in foreign capital inflows during Q1 and expectations of Selic rate cuts. Despite the bullish momentum supported by potential political changes, market analysts warn of "invisible risks" from concentrated domestic exposure, prompting recommendations for global diversification strategies.

medium.title: Petrobras (PETR4) Soars 60%, But It's Not the Only One: See Stocks That Could Surprise This Week in Money Picks
medium.summary: Petrobras emerged as a major Q1 winner with 60% gains, boosted by oil price rallies amid Iran tensions and strong dividend payments. XP maintains a buy recommendation with R$47 target, noting that each $10 Brent increase significantly impacts cash flow, though domestic fuel pricing policies that don't fully follow international parity could limit upside potential.
